_meta.source: Written for claudeDM (Sci-Fi category). Mostly original; a few general-mechanics sentences (e.g. opportunity attacks, passive checks, stat-block phrasing) are adapted from SRD 5.1, licensed CC BY 4.0 — see NOTICE.
_meta.notes: Sci-Fi backgrounds. Each carries an 'eras' tag. Money: 'equipment' holds the money line in the dollar format ('Wallet containing $40') for backgrounds usable in 1980s/modern campaigns; 'money' gives both currency forms so a generator can swap in 'Credit chit: N cr' for a credits campaign. Future-only backgrounds carry only the credits line.

backgrounds.name: Veteran
backgrounds.feature_description: You served, and that still counts for something. Other veterans and active service members will usually share a drink, a meal, a rumor or a spare magazine with you, and you can locate a former comrade in most cities with a few phone calls or messages. You can read military insignia, procedures and jargon at a glance.

backgrounds.name: Police Officer
backgrounds.feature_description: You know how a police department works from the inside. You can usually get a look at a non-sensitive report, learn who caught a case or find out whether someone has a record through an old partner or a friendly desk sergeant. Other officers tend to give you the benefit of the doubt, at least at first.

backgrounds.name: Criminal
equipment: Dark street clothes with a hood
backgrounds.feature_description: You have a reliable link to the underworld: a fence, a fixer or a cousin in a crew. Through them you can sell stolen goods, buy illegal guns and ammunition, and pass messages to criminals who would never talk to a stranger.

backgrounds.name: Academic
backgrounds.feature_description: You can get into university libraries, archives, laboratories and research databases, and other scholars will take your calls. When you don't know something, you usually know which colleague does, and can reach them within a day.

backgrounds.name: Journalist
backgrounds.feature_description: Your press pass and reputation get you into crime scenes behind the tape, press conferences, and the offices of people who want good coverage. Sources trust you to protect their names, and you know how to run a story that makes the powerful nervous.

backgrounds.name: Corporate
backgrounds.feature_description: You speak the language of boardrooms and budgets. You can get meetings with mid-level executives, understand how a company is structured and where its money goes, and bluff your way through a corporate lobby by looking like you belong.

backgrounds.name: Blue-Collar Worker
backgrounds.feature_description: Working people look out for one of their own. Dockworkers, truckers, janitors, line workers and maintenance crews will answer your questions, let you through service entrances and tell you which parts of the building the bosses don't want anyone to see.

backgrounds.name: Medical Professional
backgrounds.feature_description: You can get into hospitals and clinics without being questioned, read any medical chart, and obtain prescription drugs and medical supplies through normal channels. Doctors and nurses share information with you as a colleague.

backgrounds.name: Street Kid
equipment: Map of the city drawn from memory
backgrounds.feature_description: You know the alleys, rooftops, storm drains and shortcuts of your city. Out of combat you and your companions can travel between any two places in a city twice as fast as normal, and you can always find somewhere to sleep that nobody will look for you.

backgrounds.name: Athlete
backgrounds.feature_description: People recognize you. Fans will buy you a drink, let you jump a queue or do you a small favor for an autograph or a selfie, and you can get meetings with sponsors, coaches and the kind of rich people who like to be seen with winners.

backgrounds.name: Intelligence Agent
backgrounds.feature_description: You know how spies work: dead drops, brush passes, safe houses and counter-surveillance. You can spot someone tailing you or a room that has been searched, and you know how to reach your old agency or a rival one, though what they want in return is another matter.

backgrounds.name: Drifter
backgrounds.feature_description: You have lived out of a backpack for years. You can always find food and a safe place to sleep for yourself and up to five companions in any town or along any road, and truck stops, shelters and roadside bars are full of people who remember you kindly.

backgrounds.name: Spacer Crew
equipment: Ship's patch from your last berth
backgrounds.feature_description: You can work your passage on most commercial vessels and stations, and dockhands, pilots and ship's crew treat you as one of their own. You know which stations have honest harbormasters and which captains pay on time.

backgrounds.name: Colonist
equipment: Seed packet or keepsake from home
backgrounds.feature_description: You grew up on a raw world where everyone did their share. Colonists everywhere will offer you food, shelter and honest help, and you know how to keep pressure domes sealed, water reclaimers running and crops alive in hostile soil.
